entries.def:
σκύλλω 
__1. in cl., to skin, flay, rend (Æsch., Anthol.). 
__2. In Hellenistic writers, to vex, trouble, annoy: with accusative of person(s), Mrk.5.35, Luk.8.49; pass., ἐσκυλμένοι, distressed, Mat.9.36 mid., to trouble oneself, μὴ σκύλλου, Luk.7.6 (frequently in π.; see MM, i, ii, and cf. M, Pr., 89; Abbott, Essays, 87; Kennedy, Sources, 82).†
(AS)

σκῦλον
(Rec. σκύλον), -ου, τό [in LXX chiefly for שָׁלָל ;] 
mostly in pl., σκίλα, arms stripped from a foe, spoils: Luk.11.22.†
(AS)

σκωληκό-βρωτος, -ον
(σκώληξ, βιβρώσκω), 
eaten of worms: Act.12.23 (cf. 2Ma.9.9, and see MM, xxiii) †
(AS)

σκώληξ, -ηκος, ὁ 
[in LXX chiefly for תּוֹלָע and cogn. forms ;] 
a worm: of the kind which preys upon dead bodies, metaphorically, of fut. punishment, Mrk.9.48 (LXX, Isa.66.24 cf. Sir.7.17, Jdt.16.17).†
(AS)

σμαράγδινος
(σμάραγδος, which see), 
__1. of emerald (Luc., V.H., ii, 11). 
__2. As in π. (Deiss., BS, 267), emerald-green: Rev.4.3 (for the construction, see Swete, in l; Zorell, see word).†
(AS)

σμάραγδος, -ου, ἡ
(and in late writers also ὁ), [in LXX: Exo.28.9 (שֹׁהַם) Exo.36.17 (Exo.39.10) (בָּרֶקֶת), Ezk.28.13 (יַהֲלֹם), etc. ;] 
emerald or other trans parent green stone (LS, see word; DB, iv, 620; Swete, Ap., 67, 288): Rev.21.19.†
(AS)

σμύρνα
(in some MSS, ζμ-; see Bl., § 3, 9), -ης, ἡ, [in LXX for מֹר ;] 
myrrh, a resinous gum used as an unguent and for em­balming: Mat.2.11, Jhn.19.39.†
(AS)

Σμύρνα (T, Ζμ-; B1., § 3, 9), -ας, ἡ 
Smyrna, an Ionian city on the Ægean: Rev.1.11; 2.8.†
Ζμύρνα, -ης, ἡ, 
Rev.1.11; 2.8 T, for Σμ-, which see (cf. B1., § 3, 9; Mayser, 204).†
(AS)

Σμύρνα (T, Ζμ-; B1., § 3, 9), -ας, ἡ 
Smyrna, an Ionian city on the Ægean: Rev.1.11; 2.8.†
Ζμύρνα, -ης, ἡ, 
Rev.1.11; 2.8 T, for Σμ-, which see (cf. B1., § 3, 9; Mayser, 204).†
(AS)

σμυρνίζω
(σιύρνα), 
__1. intrans., to be like myrrh (Diosc., i, 79). 
__2. Trans., to mingle or drug with myrrh: pass., Mrk.15.23.†
(AS)
